newsitem.title: USA: United -no free airport slots for newcomers.
newsitem.headline: United -no free airport slots for newcomers.

text.p: U.S. transportation officials should refrain from subsidizing newer airlines and honor their commitments to older carriers, United Airlines President John Edwardson said Tuesday.

Briefing reporters before testifying to a Congressional subcommittee later today, Edwardson objected to proposals to give industry newcomers free airport landing and take-off slots and to water down existing rules channeling air traffic to certain airports.

Edwardson was against any plan to broaden exemptions to the so-called "perimeter rule," which requires airlines making non-stop flights of over 1,250 miles to Washington to land at Dulles International Airport, rather than the closer National Airport.
United, a subsidiary of UAL Corp., had invested roughly $2 billion in aircraft and other equipment at Dulles airport since it opened in the early 1960s, Edwardson said.
Allowing selected airlines to land at National would unfairly penalize carriers like United and renege on a promise that led to the development of Dulles, Edwardson said.
"We have made significant investments based on a rule that was made and now people want to walk away from it," he said. "We would face major costs if (the perimeter rule) is removed."

Edwardson also called on regulators to ensure open bidding on new slots at airports including Chicago's O'Hare and New York's LaGuardia and Kennedy. He called proposals to parcel them out arbitrarily as "corporate welfare" for the upstarts.
"We'd be happy to bid for new slots," Edwardson said. "That's the free market."
